question: What is the primary goal of confidentiality in healthcare computer security?

options.A: Preventing computer hardware from being stolen from the clinic
options.B: Backing up daily labor ward registers onto an external drive
options.C: Ensuring only authorized staff can view sensitive patient records
options.D: Making sure computer systems never crash during emergencies

explanation: Confidentiality focuses strictly on privacy, making certain that only people with the proper clearance can read patient information. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T4#BMP123_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why is computer security particularly critical in a midwifery or maternity clinic?

options.A: Midwives spend more time typing on computers than caring for pregnant women
options.B: Government policy requires every delivery note to be published online daily
options.C: Maternity clinics handle sensitive personal and health records of mothers and babies
options.D: Clinic computers are usually the most expensive equipment in the whole hospital

explanation: Midwifery records contain private health data and personal details that must be legally and ethically protected from outsiders. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T4#BMP123_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which type of malware locks computer files and demands payment to unlock them?
explanation: Ransomware encrypts or locks vital files on a computer and forces the user to pay a fee or meet demands to regain access. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T4#BMP123_U2_T4_h2)

question: How does a phishing attack usually target healthcare workers?

options.A: By cutting off the electrical power supply to shut down clinical servers
options.B: By intentionally spreading dust into the computer cooling fans to cause overheating
options.C: By sending fake messages designed to trick workers into revealing their passwords
options.D: By physically breaking into the labor ward at night to steal desktop computers

explanation: Phishing relies on deception, using fraudulent emails or text messages that look legitimate to steal sensitive login credentials. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T4#BMP123_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is the main function of antivirus software on a clinic computer?

options.A: To detect, block, and remove malicious software from the system
options.B: To increase the speed at which the computer connects to the internet
options.C: To prevent unauthorized people from physically stealing the computer
options.D: To automatically generate daily backups of all antenatal records

explanation: Antivirus software actively scans for harmful programs and cleans or deletes them to keep the operating system safe. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T4#BMP123_U2_T4_h3)

question: Why is keeping antivirus virus definitions updated just as important as having the software installed?

options.A: Older virus definitions take up too much physical space on the hard drive
options.B: New malware strains emerge constantly, and updates teach the software how to spot them
options.C: Software companies charge extra fines if updates are missed for more than a week
options.D: Updates are required to make the computer monitor display brighter colors

explanation: Hackers create new viruses every day, so regular updates provide the antivirus with the latest signatures needed to recognize them. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T4#BMP123_U2_T4_h3)

question: What does data backup involve in a computer system?

options.A: Installing a generator to prevent sudden power cuts in the clinic
options.B: Printing out physical paper copies of every single lab result
options.C: Making extra copies of electronic files and storing them safely elsewhere
options.D: Deleting old patient records to create more space on the hard drive

explanation: Backing up means duplicating important data so that a spare copy exists if the original is lost, stolen, or corrupted. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T4#BMP123_U2_T4_h4)

question: A clinic saves its daily delivery records on the computer hard drive and also copies them onto a flash drive kept in the same desk drawer. What is the major risk of this approach?

options.A: Storing files on a flash drive automatically deletes them after twenty-four hours
options.B: Flash drives use too much electricity and will drain the computer battery quickly
options.C: A single fire, theft, or flood in the office could destroy both the computer and the flash drive
options.D: The computer antivirus will treat the flash drive as dangerous ransomware

explanation: True data safety requires offsite or separate physical storage so that a local disaster does not wipe out all copies at once. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T4#BMP123_U2_T4_h4)

question: What should a midwife do immediately before leaving the computer terminal to attend to a patient in labor?

options.A: Shut down the main electrical generator for the clinic
options.B: Lock the computer screen to prevent unauthorized viewing
options.C: Unplug the central processing unit from the wall socket
options.D: Delete all open patient files from the desktop

explanation: Locking the screen ensures that confidential patient information remains protected while the workstation is unattended. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T4#BMP123_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why is sharing computer login passwords among clinical staff discouraged?

options.A: It violates electrical safety codes set up for hospital equipment
options.B: Password sharing automatically triggers the antivirus software alarm
options.C: It becomes impossible to track who accessed or altered specific patient records
options.D: It causes the computer operating system to slow down significantly

explanation: Unique logins ensure accountability, allowing the clinic to know exactly who viewed or edited sensitive patient data. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T4#BMP123_U2_T4_h5)
